verification_questions.question: Is the mechanism confirmed by evidence (a logged NDKPublishError / per-relay 'Timeout: 2500ms' on the failing own-send), not only inferred?
verification_questions.answer: Partly: NDK 3.0.3 source + late-ack unit tests prove the 2.5 s default; the gate snapshot (no notice, empty composer) proved a second mechanism, the blind thread-open seed.

verification_questions.question: Does a unit test that fails before the fix prove DM publishes no longer use NDK's 2.5 s default, i.e. a relay ack later than 2.5 s but within the shared timeout keeps the send successful?

Are ALL user-initiated DM publishes (text, reaction, edit/delete replacement + companion, image, delete) routed through the same timeout, with no remaining bare ndkEvent.publish() on the DM chat surface, and is the change minimal (no unrelated refactor)?

Is the timeout single-sourced and consistent with the group path (NdkNetworkAdapter.rawPublish 10 s), and does a genuine failure still roll back exactly as before (bubble removed, text restored, reaction rollback)?
Unit + tsc green via make, Stryker (concurrency 1) on changed logic, temporary diagnostics removed, full e2e gate green?
